```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
                      fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4.5)
library(data.table)
library(knitr)
source("labels.R")
source("model_tools.R")
root <- normalizePath("..")
release <- fread(file.path(root, "build/data/release.csv"))
catalog <- fread(file.path(root, "data-raw/pg_catalog.csv"), encoding = "UTF-8")
setnames(catalog, c("pg_id", "type", "issued", "catalog_title", "language",
                    "catalog_authors", "subjects", "locc", "bookshelves"))
release[catalog, on = "pg_id",
        `:=`(subjects = i.subjects, locc = i.locc, bookshelves = i.bookshelves)]
release[, genre := assign_genre(bookshelves, subjects, locc)]
release[, period25 := assign_period25(ht_year)]
release[, model_gender := assign_gender(gender)]
n_per_class <- 120L
extra <- 30L
n_year_bin <- 80L
n_gender_cell <- 25L
min_female_authors <- 20L
max_books <- 2L
n_boot <- 1000L
seed <- 20261021L
late_bins <- c("1850-1874", "1875-1899", "1900-1924")
dir.create("results", showWarnings = FALSE)
options(atlas.progress = "results/progress.log")
```

## What this pilot asks

The release is a metadata file. Its use as a corpus depends on whether the
books' texts carry the information the metadata records. This report tests
that directly. A linear model sees a passage from the middle of each book,
with the Project Gutenberg header and front matter removed, and is asked to
recover four labels.

- Broad genre: fiction, nonfiction, poetry, or drama. Books with conflicting
  or incomplete catalog signals are left out.
- Period, in three 25-year bins: 1850–1874, 1875–1899, and 1900–1924. These
  bins hold about nine in ten of the books with a standard-quality date.
- Publication year as a number, from 1800 to 1924. This avoids choosing bin
  edges and asks how many years off the model is.
- Gender, from the Wikidata claims `male` and `female`, with genre and period
  held fixed by matching.

Dates use only matched years before 1925. Earlier than 1800 there are too
few dated books to model.
Country of citizenship is not modeled; the historical labels are too
fragmented.

These fits do not update `release.csv`. A score above the baseline means the
label is predictable from the text of this corpus under the split below. It
does not mean the model has found a genre essence or an author's gender.

## Sample and split

Genre and period draw `r n_per_class` books per class. The year task draws
`r n_year_bin` books from each 25-year bin between 1800 and 1924, so the
early decades are not swamped by 1900–1924. No Project Gutenberg agent
contributes more than `r max_books` books to a class. Extra candidates are
drawn so that a book without a usable body can be replaced.

The gender sample is matched. Within each genre × 25-year cell from 1850 to
1924, the report draws `r n_gender_cell` books by women and
`r n_gender_cell` by men, and drops cells with fewer than
`r min_female_authors` women authors. Drama is left out because women
dramatists are too few before 1900. Genre and period therefore have the same
distribution in both classes and cannot produce a gender result on their
own.

Evaluation is author-disjoint. Agents are assigned to five folds, stratified
by class, and every book by an agent stays in one fold. The vocabulary, the
inverse-document-frequency weights, and the penalty are all fit on the
training folds; the penalty's inner cross-validation is also split by
author. Metrics use only held-out predictions.

```{r sample-and-fit}
prepare_pool <- function(pool, n, task_name, task_seed) {
  sampled <- sample_task(pool, "class", n, max_books, task_seed)
  sampled[, task := task_name]
  sampled
}

dated <- release[!is.na(period25)]
gender_pool <- release[!is.na(model_gender) &
                         genre %in% c("fiction", "nonfiction", "poetry") &
                         period25 %in% late_bins]
gender_pool[, cell := paste(genre, period25)]
gender_cells <- gender_pool[model_gender == "female", .(authors = uniqueN(agent)), by = cell]
gender_cells <- gender_cells[authors >= min_female_authors, cell]

candidates <- rbindlist(list(
  prepare_pool(release[genre %in% c("fiction", "nonfiction", "poetry", "drama"),
                       .(pg_id, agent, class = genre)],
               n_per_class + extra, "genre", seed),
  prepare_pool(dated[period25 %in% late_bins, .(pg_id, agent, class = period25)],
               n_per_class + extra, "period", seed + 10L),
  prepare_pool(dated[, .(pg_id, agent, class = period25, year = ht_year)],
               n_year_bin + extra, "year", seed + 30L),
  rbindlist(lapply(seq_along(gender_cells), function(i) {
    pool <- gender_pool[cell == gender_cells[[i]],
                        .(pg_id, agent, class = model_gender, cell)]
    prepare_pool(pool, n_gender_cell + 10L, "gender", seed + 100L + i)
  }))
), fill = TRUE)

views <- fetch_views(unique(candidates$pg_id), "cache/pg-text")
bge <- embed_bge(views, "cache/bge-base.csv")

usable <- function(task_name) {
  part <- views[candidates[task == task_name], on = "pg_id"]
  part[!is.na(body_text)]
}

finish_task <- function(task_name, n_keep, task_seed) {
  part <- usable(task_name)
  kept <- part[, head(.SD, n_keep), by = class]
  assign_folds(kept, "class", task_seed + 1L)
}

finish_gender <- function(task_seed) {
  part <- usable("gender")
  kept <- part[, {
    k <- min(n_gender_cell, sum(class == "female"), sum(class == "male"))
    rbind(head(.SD[class == "female"], k), head(.SD[class == "male"], k))
  }, by = cell]
  assign_folds(kept, "class", task_seed + 1L)
}

tasks <- list(
  genre = finish_task("genre", n_per_class, seed),
  period = finish_task("period", n_per_class, seed + 10L),
  year = finish_task("year", n_year_bin, seed + 30L),
  gender = finish_gender(seed + 20L)
)
outcomes <- c(genre = "class", period = "class", year = "year", gender = "class")

fwrite(rbindlist(lapply(tasks, function(t) t[, .(task, pg_id, agent, class, fold)])),
       "results/model_sample.csv")

predictions <- lapply(names(tasks), function(n) run_task(tasks[[n]], outcomes[[n]], bge))
names(predictions) <- names(tasks)
for (n in names(predictions)) {
  fwrite(predictions[[n]], sprintf("results/predictions_%s.csv", n))
}
boot <- rbindlist(lapply(names(predictions), function(n) {
  boot_task(predictions[[n]], outcomes[[n]], n_boot, seed + 500L)
}))
secondary <- lapply(names(predictions), function(n) {
  secondary_metrics(predictions[[n]], outcomes[[n]])
})
names(secondary) <- names(predictions)
fwrite(boot, "results/model_bootstrap.csv")
fwrite(rbindlist(secondary, fill = TRUE), "results/model_metrics.csv")
```

`r format(uniqueN(rbindlist(tasks, fill = TRUE)$pg_id), big.mark=",")`
distinct books were scored, from
`r format(uniqueN(candidates$pg_id), big.mark=",")` candidates. A class can
fall short of its target if too many of its texts lack a Project Gutenberg
start marker or have fewer than 1,900 words after it.

```{r sample-table}
sample_counts <- rbindlist(lapply(tasks, function(t) {
  t[, .(books = .N, authors = uniqueN(agent)), by = .(task, class)]
}))
kable(sample_counts, col.names = c("Task", "Class", "Books", "Authors"))
```

```{r gender-cells}
kable(dcast(tasks$gender[, .N, by = .(cell, class)], cell ~ class, value.var = "N"),
      col.names = c("Genre and period", "Female", "Male"),
      caption = "Matched gender sample")
```

## Text views and models

The **body view** is the evidence. It starts after the Project Gutenberg
start marker, drops the first 400 words, and takes up to 5,000 words from
the middle of what remains. That removes the header and the front matter,
where author, title, and date are concentrated. It does not remove names
inside the narrative.

The **raw view** is a check on that. It is the opening of the downloaded
file, cut to the same length as the book's body view, so it includes the
Project Gutenberg header and the title page. Digits are kept in both views,
so printed dates are visible. Because folds are author-disjoint, an author's
name on the title page cannot help with held-out books. What the raw view
can add is title wording, dates, publisher lines, and prefaces. If raw and
body score alike, the result is not coming from the cataloguing.

Each view is turned into features in two ways.

- **Word**: counts of words that occur in at least five training books,
  capped at the 8,000 most common, weighted by TF–IDF. The vocabulary is
  readable.
- **Char**: counts of character sequences three to five letters long,
  including across word boundaries, hashed into 4,096 buckets and weighted
  by TF–IDF. These pick up spelling, inflection, and function-word habits.

- **BGE**: the body view split into chunks of about 350 words, each embedded
  with `BAAI/bge-base-en-v1.5`, and averaged into one 768-dimensional vector
  per book. This is a pretrained sentence encoder rather than features fit
  to this sample. It was probably trained on some Project Gutenberg text,
  though never on these labels.

The word and character features feed an L1-penalized regression (`glmnet`,
alpha = 1, `lambda.1se`); the dense BGE vectors use the ridge form
(alpha = 0). Each is multinomial for genre and period, binomial for gender,
and linear for year.
The baseline predicts the most common training class, or the median training
year.

Macro-F1 is the unweighted mean of per-class F1, so a model that only finds
the largest class scores poorly. For year, the score is mean absolute error
in years. Intervals are 95% bootstrap intervals from `r n_boot` resamples of
authors, so an author's books are drawn together. A gain is the model's
score minus the baseline's (for year, the baseline's error minus the
model's), so a positive gain always means the text helps.

## Results

```{r results-table, results="asis"}
fmt_ci <- function(est, lo, hi, digits) {
  sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f [%.", digits, "f, %.", digits, "f]"), est, lo, hi)
}
labels <- c(baseline = "Baseline", raw_word = "Raw, word", raw_char = "Raw, char",
            body_word = "Body, word", body_char = "Body, char",
            body_bge = "Body, BGE")
for (n in names(predictions)) {
  b <- boot[task == n]
  digits <- if (outcomes[[n]] == "year") 1 else 3
  rows <- data.table(model = names(labels), Model = unname(labels))
  rows[, Score := vapply(model, function(m) {
    r <- b[quantity == m]; fmt_ci(r$estimate, r$lo, r$hi, digits)
  }, character(1))]
  rows[, Gain := vapply(model, function(m) {
    r <- b[quantity == paste0("gain_", m)]
    if (!nrow(r)) "" else fmt_ci(r$estimate, r$lo, r$hi, digits)
  }, character(1))]
  extra_col <- secondary[[n]][match(rows$model, model)]
  if (outcomes[[n]] == "year") {
    rows[, r := round(extra_col$r, 2)]
    names_out <- c("Model", "Mean abs. error, years [95% CI]", "Gain [95% CI]", "Correlation")
  } else {
    rows[, ba := round(extra_col$balanced_accuracy, 3)]
    names_out <- c("Model", "Macro-F1 [95% CI]", "Gain [95% CI]", "Balanced accuracy")
  }
  cat("\n\n### ", n, "\n\n", sep = "")
  print(kable(rows[, -1], col.names = names_out))
}
```

## Reading the results

```{r reading, results="asis"}
get_q <- function(n, q) boot[task == n & quantity == q]
ci_text <- function(r, digits) {
  sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f (95%% CI %.", digits, "f to %.", digits, "f)"),
          r$estimate, r$lo, r$hi)
}
signal_line <- function(n) {
  year <- outcomes[[n]] == "year"
  digits <- if (year) 1 else 3
  base <- get_q(n, "baseline")
  bw <- get_q(n, "body_word")
  bc <- get_q(n, "body_char")
  gw <- get_q(n, "gain_body_word")
  gc <- get_q(n, "gain_body_char")
  hw <- get_q(n, "header_word")
  ge <- get_q(n, "gain_body_bge")
  what <- if (year) "Mean absolute error in years" else "Macro-F1"
  first <- sprintf(
    "**%s.** %s is %.*f for the baseline, %s for body words, and %s for body characters.",
    n, what, digits, base$estimate, ci_text(bw, digits), ci_text(bc, digits))
  verdict <- if (gw$lo > 0 || gc$lo > 0) {
    word_best <- gw$estimate >= gc$estimate
    sprintf("The text carries this label: the gain over the baseline for body %s is %s, and the interval excludes zero.",
            if (word_best) "words" else "characters",
            ci_text(if (word_best) gw else gc, digits))
  } else {
    "The gain over the baseline has an interval that includes zero, so this sample does not show a stable signal in the text."
  }
  header <- if (hw$lo > 0) {
    sprintf("The raw opening adds %s on top of the body words, so part of the raw-view score comes from the header and front matter.",
            ci_text(hw, digits))
  } else if (hw$hi < 0) {
    "The body words do better than the raw opening, so the header is not where the signal lies."
  } else {
    "The raw opening and the body words do about equally well, so the header adds nothing measurable."
  }
  embed <- sprintf("BGE embeddings of the same passage give a gain of %s.",
                   ci_text(ge, digits))
  paste(first, verdict, embed, header)
}
cat(paste(vapply(names(predictions), signal_line, character(1)), collapse = "\n\n"))
```

Gender is matched on genre and period, but not on everything that travels
with gender in this corpus, such as subject matter within nonfiction or the
kinds of books by women that were reprinted and digitized. A gender result
here should not be described as a detector of gendered language.

## Confusion matrices

Rows are the true class and columns the predicted class, summed over the
five held-out folds. The last column is the recall for that row. For the
year task, the predicted year is placed in the same 25-year bins.

```{r confusion, results="asis"}
for (n in names(predictions)) {
  pred <- copy(predictions[[n]])
  if (outcomes[[n]] == "year") {
    for (m in models_in(pred)[-1]) {
      p <- pmin(pmax(pred[[m]], 1800), 1924)
      set(pred, j = m, value = assign_period25(round(p)))
    }
  }
  cat("\n\n### ", n, " {.tabset}\n\n", sep = "")
  for (m in c("body_word", "body_char", "body_bge", "raw_word", "raw_char")) {
    cat("\n\n#### ", labels[[m]], "\n\n", sep = "")
    tab <- as.data.table(table(Actual = pred$class,
                               Predicted = factor(pred[[m]], levels = sort(unique(pred$class)))))
    wide <- dcast(tab, Actual ~ Predicted, value.var = "N", fill = 0)
    counts <- as.matrix(wide[, -1])
    wide[, recall := round(diag(counts) / rowSums(counts), 2)]
    print(kable(wide, caption = sprintf("%s, %s", n, labels[[m]])))
  }
}
```

A transformer is not part of this run. It would be worth fitting where the
linear body-text model already clears the baseline, as a check on how much
a stronger encoder adds. It would not change the release.
